canonical_statement: The study tests whether embedding-mediated top-k retrieval is structurally ill-suited to exactness-critical, long, densely tabular documents and whether direct deterministic document operations provide a better retrieval interface.

The comparison holds the document and generator backbone constant while changing the retrieval interface: embedding-mediated top-k versus deterministic search, structure navigation, and bounded span reads.
READ composes normalized line search, document outline navigation, and bounded span reads in an iterative tool loop whose operations return inspectable line locations.
READ is implemented as a read-only MCP server over Markdown with four tools: list, outline, grep, and read; paths are jailed to a root directory and reads are hard-capped.
The converted report contains 19,198 non-empty lines, of which 16,664 are table rows, corresponding to a table-row fraction of 86.8%.

The table-aware chunker scans backward at each chunk boundary for the nearest unit declaration and nearest fiscal-year or as-at-date header, then prepends those context lines within a bounded seed budget.

Normalized matching creates spaced and squashed shadow forms using Unicode normalization, case folding, emphasis stripping, table-boundary handling, whitespace collapse, and removal of thousands separators for squashed matching.
Among twelve realistic matching probes, normalization changed the retrieval outcome for exactly two probes: an ungrouped numeric figure and a phrase split across table cells.

canonical_statement: The paper treats conversion-limited questions as a separate benchmark category because a retriever cannot recover evidence that the PDF-to-Markdown conversion has already destroyed.

Four PDF-to-Markdown backends were compared before retrieval-system construction; pymupdf4llm was selected because it preserved row labels with their figures across table columns, while the tested alternatives had more structurally destructive failures or did not complete.
The converter comparison is a one-document, non-blinded judgement by readers who knew which backend they were already using, so it is not presented as a general converter benchmark.
The evaluation benchmark contains 51 verified questions across six categories: 24 lookups, 9 arithmetic, 6 navigation, 5 aggregation, 5 unanswerable, and 2 conversion-limited questions.

canonical_statement: All compared systems use Gemini 2.5 Pro as the generator; dense retrieval uses BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 and hybrid retrieval adds cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2.
The critical AgenticVec/agentic-RAG control gives the same iterative agent loop and budget a vector-search top-k tool instead of READ operations, isolating interface effects from iteration effects.

Gold answers are transcribed by the authors and then mechanically checked for evidence presence, table-column consistency via arithmetic identities where available, and non-occurrence of derived answers in the corpus.
Exact-figure accuracy uses deterministic numeric comparison with normalization for Indian digit grouping, parenthesized negatives, and lakh/crore units at 0.5% relative tolerance.
Groundedness is defined mechanically as whether every figure in an answer appears in text the system actually retrieved or read.
System comparisons are paired by question using exact McNemar tests on discordant pairs, paired bootstrap intervals for accuracy differences, and Holm correction across the family of baselines.
The benchmark contains 32 hard, 13 medium, and 6 easy questions; 10 questions have derived answers, and 14 questions have all evidence after printed page 100.

In the two-question pilot, the dense baseline abstained because its top-k context did not contain both operands 47 lines apart, whereas READ located both operands and computed the unprinted difference.

A provisional provenance error in the pilot was traced to the authors’ section-attribution code rather than the model; the paper reports this as an example of analysis-layer bugs manufacturing plausible model-behavior findings.
READ answered 58.8% of the 51-question benchmark, with a Wilson 95% interval of 45.2% to 71.2%.

The study evaluates one converted financial report, one generator backbone, and 51 questions, so transfer to other document classes, accounting conventions, converters, and weaker models is not established.
With 51 questions, the benchmark is designed to resolve only large paired differences; the approximately 7.8-point READ-BM25 gap is unresolved rather than demonstrated absent.
The benchmark was authored by the same group that built READ, creating a risk that task construction favors the system under test even though gold answers receive mechanical checks.

The benchmark expanded after inspection of an earlier 25-question experiment; although additions targeted coverage defects rather than observed per-system outcomes, the growth was not preregistered and the authors knew the hypothesized failure mode.
READ did not demonstrate superior groundedness: its groundedness rate was lower than BM25 and hybrid, weakening a broad interpretability claim.
The converter-induced error ceiling and unit-header distances are specific to this report and pymupdf4llm conversion; other documents and converters may shift both.
READ presumes lexical anchors that share surface vocabulary with the evidence; tasks with stronger paraphrase mismatch may favor dense or hybrid retrieval.
READ has variable per-query cost and can substantially exceed fixed top-k retrieval cost and latency, so the reported accuracy/auditability trade-off may not suit high-volume search.

For this exactness-critical structured document, the authors conclude that a fixed partition is the wrong primitive when meaning depends on inherited layout context and the required context is query-dependent.
The authors conclude that the observed gain is attributable to retrieval interface rather than iteration because the same agent loop with a vector top-k tool reached only 27.5%.
The paper explicitly does not claim that embeddings are obsolete or that dense retrieval is generally weak; its supported scope is long structured documents where inherited layout context matters.
